### Power Play
Author: Stuart Briscoe
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/one-year-devotions-for-men/power-play-one-year-devotions-for-men-july-24.html
Passage: Numbers 16:1-3
Points:
- Political intrigue and power struggles often stem from craving prestige rather than serving others.
- Korah cloaked his selfish ambitions behind pious language of equality among God's people.
- Although all Israel belonged to God, the Lord sovereignly assigned distinct roles within the community.
- Resisting God's delegated leadership is fundamentally a revolt against God Himself.
- Believers must embrace their appointed callings instead of grasping for authority that is not theirs.

### God Anoints and Appoints
Author: Daily Disciples Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/daily-disciples/daily-disciples-devotional-feb-27-2009-11600132.html
Passage: Numbers 16:1-3
Points:
- Envy and jealousy lead people to criticize leaders whom God has established.
- Challenging appointed leaders amounts to questioning God's wisdom and sovereign choice.
- The Holy Spirit distributes varied callings, some in public view and others in quiet obscurity.
- Critical thoughts must be taken captive before they cultivate bitterness, pride, and open rebellion.
- Believers must respect God's placements so they do not miss His work in their own lives.

### Devotional: Numbers 16
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/numbers-16-psalms-52-54-isaiah-6-hebrews-13/
Passage: Numbers 16:1-22
Points:
- Korah and his cohort leveraged popular desert hardships to stir resentment against Moses.
- The rebels disguised a naked lust for power behind egalitarian religious rhetoric.
- Discontented hearts quickly forget past deliverance and distort God's revealed truth.
- Genuine biblical reform stands on submission to God's Word rather than manipulating it for selfish ends.
- Rebelling against the Lord's holy order invites severe divine judgment.

### Bible Pathways 2/20/2004
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathways-2-or-20-or-2004-1243557.html
Passage: Numbers 16:2-3
Points:
- Prominent tribal leaders were swayed by persuasive arguments that disguised open rebellion.
- Korah was privileged with sacred Levite duties but became dissatisfied because he wanted higher recognition.
- Serving God solely for public acclaim and status corrupts spiritual ministry.
- Scripture treats murmuring against appointed spiritual leaders as an offense directly against God.
- Believers are called to godly humility and willing submission to delegated authorities.
